title: Spoken English
modules: Parameters For Classification Of The English Vowels
mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the peculiar possession of humans."
Language so defined is the peculiar possession of humans.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a certain pattern, not an arbitrary one, because it is meaningful in discourse."
A tune is a certain pattern, not an arbitrary one, because it is meaningful in discourse.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is used to express request, warning, normal apologies, reservations, encouragement and a few other specialized sentences."
The falling-rising tune is used to express request, warning, normal apologies, reservations, encouragement and a few other specialized sentences.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a human language in which the words are uttered through the mouth."
A spoken language is a human language in which the words are uttered through the mouth.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an ever evolving process on planet Earth varying from culture to culture and place to place depending on the needs of the civilization that existed at that timeline."
Language is an ever evolving process on planet Earth varying from culture to culture and place to place depending on the needs of the civilization that existed at that timeline.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the grammatical changes that occur at the endings of English words."
Inflection refers to the grammatical changes that occur at the endings of English words.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is used to refer to the fear of public speaking."
Glossophobia is used to refer to the fear of public speaking.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are used by people who are deaf or hearing-impaired."
Sign languages are used by people who are deaf or hearing-impaired.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are those organs that cannot move; for example, the organs of the roof of the mouth (Elugbe 2000:21)."
Passive articulators are those organs that cannot move; for example, the organs of the roof of the mouth (Elugbe 2000:21).

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a language which uses gestures, motion and expression instead of sound to convey meaning: combinations of hand shapes, movements of the hands, arms or body, and facial expressions."
A sign language is a language which uses gestures, motion and expression instead of sound to convey meaning: combinations of hand shapes, movements of the hands, arms or body, and facial expressions.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is defined as a ranking of speech sounds (or phones) by how much 'sound' they produce (Wikipedia.org)."
Sonority hierarchy otherwise known sonority scale is defined as a ranking of speech sounds (or phones) by how much 'sound' they produce (Wikipedia.org).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a single sound made with the free flow of air from the lungs out of the mouth (oral cavity)."
An English monophthong or simple vowel is a single sound made with the free flow of air from the lungs out of the mouth (oral cavity).

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a strongly stressed language, in that certain syllables, both within words and within phrases, get a relative prominence/loudness during pronunciation while the others do not."
English is a strongly stressed language, in that certain syllables, both within words and within phrases, get a relative prominence/loudness during pronunciation while the others do not.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the core of the syllable, and is obligatory in all languages."
The nucleus is the core of the syllable, and is obligatory in all languages.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are known to be strong or stressed syllables while weak or unstressed syllables are produced with relatively weaker little force (Elugbe 2000: 135)."
Syllables pronounced with greater force are known to be strong or stressed syllables while weak or unstressed syllables are produced with relatively weaker little force (Elugbe 2000: 135).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a bit more difficult than describing consonants."
Describing vowels is a bit more difficult than describing consonants.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is one of the organs here, and may be described as the most active articulator."
The tongue is one of the organs here, and may be described as the most active articulator.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is concerned with the actual speech sounds of human languages; how they are pronounced by moving various organs in the vocal tract, perceived by the human ear and their physical properties."

Speech production is concerned with the actual speech sounds of human languages; how they are pronounced by moving various organs in the vocal tract, perceived by the human ear and their physical properties.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the sound that ends the syllable; it is optional in some languages, but is highly restricted in others."
The coda is the sound that ends the syllable; it is optional in some languages, but is highly restricted in others.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the smallest unit into which a word can be divided."
A syllable is the smallest unit into which a word can be divided.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the voiceless glottal fricative sound which is produced as the flow of air passes through an open glottis to the oral cavity."
The / h / consonant is the voiceless glottal fricative sound which is produced as the flow of air passes through an open glottis to the oral cavity.
fib: ______ is a matter of competence with a writing system and with the specialized functions that written language serves in a particular society.
Literacy
Literacy is a matter of competence with a writing system and with the specialized functions that written language serves in a particular society.
______ may be defined as any conventional system of marks or signs that represents the utterances of a language.
writing system
A writing system may be defined as any conventional system of marks or signs that represents the utterances of a language.
______ is considered primary because every normal human being possesses the natural ability to speak, unlike writing which is a more deliberate skill that has to be systematically taught and learned.
Speech
Speech is considered primary because every normal human being possesses the natural ability to speak, unlike writing which is a more deliberate skill that has to be systematically taught and learned.
______ is any vocal sound that can be made continuously with no blockage of the oral cavity.
vowel
A vowel is any vocal sound that can be made continuously with no blockage of the oral cavity.
______ is a form of human communication by means of a set of visible marks that are related, by convention, to some particular structural level of language.
Writing
Writing is a form of human communication by means of a set of visible marks that are related, by convention, to some particular structural level of language.
______ are those organs in the vocal tract that can move freely; for example, the tongue.
Active articulators
Active articulators are those organs in the vocal tract that can move freely; for example, the tongue.
______ is the continuation of the roof of the mouth also called the palate.
velum
The velum is the continuation of the roof of the mouth also called the palate.
______ is one of the more important determiners of stress.
Length
Length is one of the more important determiners of stress.
______ are the easiest, because most of them have the same form as a letter of the alphabet (17 out of 24).
consonants
The consonants are the easiest, because most of them have the same form as a letter of the alphabet (17 out of 24).
______ are the key words of a sentence, because they are the important words that carry the meaning or sense of the sentence.
Content words
Content words are the key words of a sentence, because they are the important words that carry the meaning or sense of the sentence.
______ is the opening between the vocal folds.
glottis
The glottis is the opening between the vocal folds.
______ is a speech sound that is produced by a partial or complete blockage of the flow of air from the lungs by any of the speech organs.
consonant
A consonant is a speech sound that is produced by a partial or complete blockage of the flow of air from the lungs by any of the speech organs.
______ is a phonetic element that normally patterns as a consonant, but may fill a vowel slot in a syllable.
syllabic consonant
A syllabic consonant is a phonetic element that normally patterns as a consonant, but may fill a vowel slot in a syllable.
______ refer to the accentual patterns on sentences.
Intonation tunes
Intonation tunes refer to the accentual patterns on sentences.
______ refers to where in the vocal tract a particular sound is produced.
Place of articulation
Place of articulation refers to where in the vocal tract a particular sound is produced.
______ is used at the end of a list to show that the list is complete.
falling tone
A falling tone is used at the end of a list to show that the list is complete.
______ is a single sound composed of a stop portion and a fricative portion.
affricate
An affricate is a single sound composed of a stop portion and a fricative portion.
______ is used in question which demand only a 'yes' or 'no' answer (polar question).
rising tune
The rising tune is used in question which demand only a 'yes' or 'no' answer (polar question).
______ is an auditory sensation that places sounds on a scale from high to low.
Pitch
Pitch is an auditory sensation that places sounds on a scale from high to low.
______ is the representation of a language by means of a writing system.
written language
A written language is the representation of a language by means of a writing system.
According to the course material, how many types of closures that can be observed are there? (answer in figures)
three

There are three types of closures that can be observed; bilabial (bringing the two lips together), alveolar (placing the tongue blade against the alveolar ridge) and velar (placing the back of the tongue against the palate).
